scope: the two cursor fields are SELF-CONSISTENT (byte 163, bit offset 3) and that consistency confirms the id/count overlap is a REAL format contradiction, not a measurement artefact

the_self_consistency_check.observed: 1307 = 1304 + 3, i.e. byte 163 with a bit offset of 3
the_self_consistency_check.verdict: consistent - the two fields describe the SAME position (bit 1307 = byte 163 bit 3), with [+0x1C] naming the NEXT byte to read

why_that_matters: it removes the last possibility that the id/count collision was an artefact of misreading the fields
so in OUR body the count is read from byte 164 while the 12-bit id occupies bits 1309..1320, which live in bytes 163-165
the two really do overlap, which a working format cannot allow
the_conclusion_for_the_format: either the header must end on a byte boundary so that the gates and the id start at byte 164 (position 1312), or
the count is not a whole byte in the real format and 0x66ED70 is used for a different message
the first option is far more likely because 0x66ED70 is unambiguously a whole-byte reader and the gates are unambiguously bit reads
the_concrete_next_experiment: shift the entity block start from 1307 to 1312 by making the header 1312 bits: take the hybrid prefix, pad it with 5 zero bits at the end of the header, then place the gates at 1312/1313
the ps block then begins at 1313, which is harmless because our ps block decodes nothing anyway
and the count byte stays at 164, so count and id no longer collide
